message.content:
Based on my search, here is a comprehensive overview of BMI standards:

## What is BMI?

Body Mass Index (BMI) is a screening tool that estimates body fat using a person's weight relative to their height. It is calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared (kg/m²).

---

## Standard BMI Classifications (WHO/NIH - Used for White, Hispanic, and Black populations)

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight | Less than 18.5 |
| Normal/Healthy Weight | 18.5 to 24.9 |
| Overweight | 25.0 to 29.9 |
| Obesity Class I | 30.0 to 34.9 |
| Obesity Class II | 35.0 to 39.9 |
| Obesity Class III (Severe Obesity) | 40.0 or greater |

---

## Asian-Specific BMI Standards

Due to higher metabolic risk at lower body weights, the WHO and NIH have established lower thresholds for Asian populations:

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight | Less than 18.5 |
| Normal | 18.5 to 22.9 |
| Overweight | 23.0 to 24.9 |
| Obesity | 25.0 or greater |

---

## China's Adult BMI Standards

According to China's national standard (WS/T428-2013):

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight (体重过低) | Less than 18.5 |
| Normal (体重正常) | 18.5 to 23.9 |
| Overweight (超重) | 24.0 to 27.9 |
| Obesity (肥胖) | 28.0 or greater |

---

## Special Populations

| Population | Recommended BMI Range |
|------------|----------------------|
| **Elderly (general)** | 20.0 to 26.9 kg/m² |
| **Adults aged 80+** | 22.0 to 26.9 kg/m² |

---

## Important Limitations

BMI is a screening measure, not a diagnostic tool. It does not:
- Distinguish between muscle and fat mass
- Account for body fat distribution
- Apply to pregnant women, children/teens (use age/sex-specific percentiles), or very muscular individuals

For a more complete health assessment, BMI should be considered alongside other measures such as **waist circumference**, **body fat percentage**, blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood glucose levels.

---

## How to Calculate BMI

**Metric formula:** BMI = weight (kg) ÷ [height (m)]²

**Imperial formula:** BMI = [weight (lbs) × 703] ÷ [height (in)]²

---

Sources:
1. https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/9464-body-mass-index-bmi
2. https://www.heart.org/en/healthy-living/healthy-eating/losing-weight/bmi-in-adults
3. https://www.myheart.org.sg/tools-resources/bmi-calculator/
4. https://www.uptodate.com/contents/image?imageKey=OBGYN%2F97661
5. http://www.nhc.gov.cn/ylyjs/s3573d/202412/4cf1905d32304c15ac3bc4446ddb83f1/files/f932c5c0004f4959b92613dd1024483c.pdf
6. http://dayi.org.cn/qa/279026
7. https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkkp/mxfcrb/lnjk/202408/t20240823_295135.html
8. https://www.cdc.gov/bmi/adult-calculator/bmi-categories.html
9. https://apps.who.int/nutrition/landscape/help.aspx?menu=0&helpid=420
10. https://bmicalculatorweb.com/blog/who-new-bmi-classification-obesity-diagnosis-criteria.html
